🌋✨ Did You Know? Mount Apo Is More Than Just a Mountain!

Standing tall at 2,938 meters, Mount Apo is not only the highest peak in the Philippines—it’s also a potentially active volcano.

Located along the powerful Pacific Ring of Fire, the Philippines is shaped by intense geological activity. Mount Apo itself is classified as a stratovolcano, quietly holding signs of life beneath its surface.

Although it has no recorded eruptions, nature leaves clues—sulfuric vents, steaming fumaroles, hidden craters, and nearby hot springs—all pointing to ongoing magmatic activity deep below. 🌫️🔥

And it’s not alone. Other iconic peaks like Mount Arayat, Mount Makiling, and Mount Banahaw also share volcanic origins.

Air Quality Update 

QCitizens, pinapayuhan ang lahat na manatili muna sa loob ng bahay hangga’t maaari.

Nananatiling “Unhealthy” at “Very Unhealthy” ang kalidad ng hangin sa Quezon City base sa Air Quality Index (AQI) ngayong 2:00PM. 

Ito ay posibleng dulot ng usok mula sa sunog sa Navotas Landfill na pinalalala rin ng thermal inversion (pagka-trap ng polusyon malapit sa lupa). 

Kung di maiiwasan ang pag-alis, lalo na sa mga senior citizens, buntis at may respiratory diseases tulad ng hika, huwag kalimutang magsuot ng face mask.

Para sa karagdagang impormasyon tungkol sa AQI, maaaring makipag-ugnayan sa Climate Change and Environmental Sustainability Department (CCESD) 
https://t.co/q1RzmvzoZq

Para sa health concerns tulad ng hirap sa paghinga, hika, at iba pa, maaaring tumawag sa City Health Department sa Tel. No. (02) 8929-8038. 

Maaari ring tumawag sa QC Helpline 122 para sa iba pang agarang aksyon.
